newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish near steady in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish near steady in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished near steady in thin trading as players turned wary ahead of Friday's September jobs data.
December Treasury bond futures popped to a six-week high early in the day, then cut their gains after the early aggressive buying faded, traders said.

"There's been some good buyers of U.S. securities, but I'm a little bit wary going into tomorrow," a futures analyst said. "Volume turned relatively light and there was really nothing much on the flow side in the last hour," he said.
September non-farm payrolls was forecast up 166,000, compared with a 250,000 gain in August. That report will be released at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT on Friday.
"I'm optimistic but on the other hand my logic tells me not to be because we've had a good run up and I don't like to get long ahead of big numbers after a run-up," the analyst said.

December T-bonds have crawled above resistance at 110-2/32 and 110-10/32 this week to reach a new six-week high at 110-26/32 on pre-jobs report bullish momentum. The trend faltered near midday, with December closing on former resistance of 110-10/32 for the second consecutive session.
With all eyes on Friday's employment report, traders said light sideways action late today was inevitable.
Some said they expected minimal reaction to the number on Friday unless jobs rose 100,000 or less or 250,000 or more. Otherwise, rangetrade could ensue, they said.

The unemployment rate was forecast at 5.2 percent, compared with 5.1 percent in August. Average hourly earnings were forecast up 0.2 percent and the average September workweek was pegged at 34.5 hours.
Data early on Thursday had scant impact on futures.
The latest weekly jobless claims were reported unchanged at 340,000, and August factory orders fell 1.9 percent.

December Treasury bond futures ended unchanged at 110-10/32, muni-bonds finished up 3/32 at 115-8/32, and March Euros were down 1 basis point at 94.18. March T-bills were down 3 basis points at 94.70.
